text:
eric_support: Heads up — ACME (tenant acme-42) opened a support ticket: sudden p99 jump on /v1/generate in us-west-2 after the staggered-batcher rollout at ~18:22 UTC. No 5xx, just high tail latency. sample req: req_0a1b2c3d. Panel: https://grafana.redwood/acme/reqs

jason_sre: thanks. which model/route and any related errors in logs (auth/billing/429)?

eric_support: model=redwood/gpt-smallv2, route=/v1/generate. No 429/503, client reports responses taking 1.5-2.2s (p99). Grafana link above.

priya_eng: this smells like the new staggered ramp config for continuous-batcher. We increased max_hold_ms on ramp-up shards to 25ms and introduced a stagger window. That can cause lots of size=1 batches to sit longer when traffic is bursty/tiny. Can you paste a few batch logs?

eric_support: small log snip from the node serving acme-42:
```
[2024-12-01T18:23:05Z] batch_id=0x7a3 tenant=acme-42 size=1 hold_ms=42 processing_ms=18 total_ms=60
[2024-12-01T18:23:06Z] batch_id=0x7a4 tenant=acme-42 size=1 hold_ms=48 processing_ms=20 total_ms=72
[2024-12-01T18:23:07Z] batch_id=0x7a5 tenant=acme-42 size=1 hold_ms=50 processing_ms=19 total_ms=69
```

priya_eng: yep, hold_ms >> processing_ms and size=1 dominant. Staggered ramp added an extra jitter delay to smooth GPU handoff but for very small prompts this amplifies tail.

alex_platform: mitigation options (quick):
- reduce staggered max_hold_ms from 25 -> 8 for tiny-input routes
- add per-tenant override to disable staggered ramp for acme-42
- enable aggressive prefix cache & smaller microbatch window (min_coalesce_ms=2)
- route acme to dedicated pool (if available)

jason_sre: can we repro locally? need repro steps to schedule a quick canary rollback.

eric_support: repro script the customer ran (they sent):
```bash
KEY=xxx
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```
They said increasing client concurrency made tail worse, which matches hold backlog.

priya_eng: For immediate remediation I recommend:
1) apply per-route override: set continuous_batcher.staggered_ramp.enabled=false for /v1/generate on acme-42
2) set continuous_batcher.max_hold_ms=8 globally for us-west-2 for the next hour
3) enable prefix cache for small prompt routes
That should bring p99 down quickly. We'll follow up with a safer rollout (gradual ramp, tenant heuristics).

marco_support: Customer on the call can accept a short config rollback if it reduces latency. They want a canary first.

jason_sre: I'll push a 10% canary rollback to disable staggered_ramp for acme-42 in us-west-2 now. @sre-bot kick off canary job.

sre-bot: Deploy job started: canary=10% target=us-west-2 override=continuous_batcher.staggered_ramp.enabled:false (job id: deploy-7731)

(some minutes pass)

sre-bot: Deploy job success: deploy-7731 completed in 00:03:12. Monitoring p95/p99 now.

jason_sre: early check — p99 for acme-42 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~340ms within 5m on canary hosts. p95 ~120ms -> ~110ms. still verifying for longer tail.

eric_support: customer confirmed noticeable improvement on the canary traffic. They want a full rollback in us-west-2 while engineering designs a graduated ramp with per-tenant heuristics.

priya_eng: followups:
- create a regression test that simulates 500 tiny-req burst under staggered ramp and records p95/p99
- add a config knob min_batch_size_threshold to skip staggered ramp when size==1 for small prompt routes
- document recommended defaults for continuous_batcher for public customers (max_hold_ms <= 10 for small prompts)

jason_sre: filing infra ticket to roll back across us-west-2 and schedule a postmortem. I'll link the ticket here.

eric_support: ticket created: https://support.redwood/tickets/ACME-842. Closing the escalation once full rollback is confirmed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
